author: Temminck, 1831
status: 나그네새 10만 마리 이상 · 겨울철새 수천 마리
summary: 우리나라에서 겨울을 나는 지빠귀로, 평지나 산지의 숲속에 산다. 주로 식물의 열매를 먹고 지렁이와 벌레도 좋아한다. 시베리아 북부와 캄차카반도에서 번식하며, 5~6월에 나뭇가지 위에 잔 모양 둥지를 틀고 알을 4~7개 낳는다.

points.en: white breast, belly and flanks spotted black

art.subject: Dusky Thrush (Turdus eunomus), adult male in fresh winter plumage, as seen in Korean woodland from October to March: crown, nape and ear-coverts blackish-brown, forming a dark cap and cheek patch; long, broad creamy-white supercilium; whitish chin and throat bordered by a thin blackish malar stripe; mantle and back dark brown with blackish feather centres; wing coverts and flight-feather edges extensively rufous-chestnut, forming a rufous panel on the closed wing (the amount of rufous varies between individuals); underparts white with a band of dense black spots across the breast, a whiter gap below it, and bold black spots along the flanks; belly and undertail coverts white; tail dark brown. Bill blackish with a yellow base to the lower mandible; dark brown eye; pale pinkish-brown legs.
art.pose: perched on a bare branch, side view
art.scene: Korean winter woodland on a low hill; no people, buildings or text
views: adult male, winter, side view perched on a branch: blackish-brown cap and ear-coverts, long creamy-white supercilium and whitish throat, dark brown upperparts, rufous-chestnut panel on the closed wing, white underparts with a black-spotted breast band and black-spotted flanks, pale legs
adult male, head detail in side view: long creamy-white supercilium, blackish ear-coverts, whitish throat with a thin black malar stripe, dark bill with a yellow base to the lower mandible

adult female or first-winter, side view standing on the ground: the same pattern but duller and browner with less contrast, buffier supercilium and throat, less rufous in the wing and sparser breast spotting
art.build: Medium-sized thrush, 23cm, a little smaller and much shorter-tailed than a Brown-eared Bulbul and clearly larger than a sparrow; plump and deep-chested, stands upright with the head raised and hops on the ground. Rounded head, short neck. Bill straight, fairly stout, slightly shorter than the head, the culmen curving down gently at the tip. Legs medium-long and sturdy, pale pinkish-brown. At rest the wingtips reach just past the base of the tail. Tail medium length, square-ended, dark brown. In flight the underwing coverts are rufous-chestnut.
avoid: Do not paint orange-rufous spots on the underparts or rufous tail sides — that is Naumann's Thrush (Turdus naumanni); the Dusky Thrush is spotted black on white.
Do not paint a plain grey or brown head without the long pale supercilium and dark cheek patch.
Do not paint an orange breast or unspotted white underparts.
Do not give it dark grey or black legs; they are pale pinkish-brown.
